title: A big name on a small balance sheet
lede: FAO Schwarz was privately owned for almost all of its life, so its own accounts are not public. The two years it spent inside a listed company, FAO Inc., are documented in SEC filings, and most of the figures below come from them. Earlier figures come from a reference history and are marked.

blocks.title: FAO Schwarz stores: one, many, one
blocks.subtitle: Store counts at the dates a source gives one. The spacing is not even.
blocks.xLabel: Date of the count (not evenly spaced)

points.title: the first chain
points.text: 32 stores under Franz Carl Weber, some in hotel lobbies. Ten were closed as unprofitable (the 22 is derived).[^9]

points.title: the Vendex peak
points.text: “More than 40” stores, plotted as 40, with estimated sales of $197M in 2000.[^9]

points.title: the sale
points.text: The Right Start buys the flagship and 22 other stores.[^1]

points.title: after the first bankruptcy
points.text: 15 stores in 12 states. Eight were closed in Chapter 11.[^1]

points.title: after the second
points.text: Only New York and Las Vegas reopen under D. E. Shaw.[^8][^17]

points.title: the end of the original
points.text: The Fifth Avenue store closes on July 15, 2015.[^22]

points.title: the revival
points.text: One new flagship at 30 Rockefeller Plaza. Partner-run stores abroad are not counted here.[^29][^30]

blocks.source: 32, 39 and “more than 40”: International Directory of Company Histories[^9]. 23 and 15: FAO Inc. 10-K reports[^1][^2]. Two stores in 2004[^8][^17]. One store at January 30, 2010: Toys “R” Us 10-K[^21]. Closing and reopening: Associated Press[^22][^29]. The 22 for about 1985 is derived (32 − 10) and its date is approximate.
